newsitem.title: UK: UK managers doubt Labour economic competence - poll.
newsitem.headline: UK managers doubt Labour economic competence - poll.

text.p: Britain's company managers believe the opposition Labour party is more in touch with the needs of business than it used to be, but they doubt its competence in economic policy, according to a poll by the Institute of Management.
Its survey of 386 managers this week -- during the Labour party annual conference -- showed 56 percent believe Labour does not have a clear strategy for the economy.
Sixty percent or more said a Labour government could not be trusted to control government borrowing or spending or to keep inflation under control.
"On many key issues, managers are inclined to sing Labour's praises, but a crucial credibility gap remains," Institute of Management director-general Roger Young said.
"Labour must have a clear and costed economic strategy if it is to strike the right chord and win the business vote."
Seventy-eight percent of respondents thought income tax would be more likely to rise under a Labour government and 60 percent thought they would be less well off under Labour.

Ninety-three percent favoured full British involvement in negotiations on a single European currency. Sixty-seven percent thought a Labour government would be more likely to take Britain into a single currency.
